Items.Authors: Wengfei Liu, Mengmeng Qian, Jiahao Zhou, Haoyang Zhang, Yingfu Wang, Kai Yun, Xianke Song, Hongzhuan Hu, Jianping Wang, Jiaru Chu, Ping Zhang, Zhigang Liu, Zengxiang Zhou
Items.Title: An FPGA-based method for real-time light spot centroid extraction in fiber positioning
Items.Abstract: This paper proposes an FPGA-based real-time centroid localization algorithm for light spots to address issues such as high latency and substantial data transmission pressure in traditional processing methods for fiber positioning in the LAMOST telescope. By processing the image data stream and computing centroid coordinates in real time at the acquisition end, experiments verify that the algorithm's processing time aligns with the camera output, enabling adaptation to systems with different frame rates and achieving real-time localization.

Items.Authors: Pierre R. Nicolas, Patrick Ingraham, Heejoo Choi, Ewan S. Douglas, Solvay Blomquist, Kevin Derby, Daewook Kim
Items.Title: An open-source Python pipeline for optical performances and alignment analysis using ray-tracing tools
Items.Abstract: This paper presents a fast, accurate, and easily integratable open-source pipeline for analyzing optical system performance under mechanical and thermal perturbations. Built on the Batoid ray-tracing library, the method replaces complex multi-tool workflows with a unified Python-based framework. It processes design variations such as alignment errors, rigid-body motions, and surface deformations-imported directly from standard finite-element-analysis (FEA) outputs-and applies them to the optical model. The pipeline includes automated conversion of Zemax prescriptions, deformation ingestion, system updating, and extraction of optical diagnostics. Using a three-mirror anastigmat telescope and sample Structural-Thermal-Optical-Performance (STOP) data, the paper demonstrates the pipeline's ability to rapidly compute wavefront error, boresight shifts, optical motions, and surface deformation impacts. This approach enables fast feedback loops for design teams and accelerates the development.

Items.Authors: Matthew H. Smith, Manuel A. Quijada, Javier G. Del Hoyo, Luis V. Rodriguez de Marcos, H. Philip Stahl
Items.Title: An ultra-wideband Mueller matrix polarimeter for full-aperture mapping of 2 m-class astronomical mirrors
Items.Abstract: NASA’s Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) seeks to enable detection and characterization of Earth-sized exoplanets using coronagraphs capable of achieving contrast ratios approaching 10⁻¹⁰. Accurate control of polarization aberrations introduced by telescope mirrors and coatings is essential to meeting this requirement. We report the development of an ultra-wideband Mueller matrix polarimeter for full-aperture polarization mapping of 2 m-class astronomical mirrors. The instrument extends a dual-rotating-retarder architecture to the 250–2100 nm spectral range using hyper-achromatic retarders and a dual-detector configuration with silicon and indium gallium arsenide sensors. Integrated on a large-aperture variable-rotation reflection mount, the system supports angle-of-incidence-dependent measurements and ≤25 mm spatial sampling across the mirror surface.

Items.Authors: Gayoung Lee, Jongwan Ko, Daewook Kim, Yunjong Kim, Jihun Kim, Woowon Byun, Kyohoon Ahn, Dohoon Kim
Items.Title: Analysis of mid-to-high spatial frequency surface errors in off-axis freeform three mirror system
Items.Abstract: We present the development and on-sky performance of the KASI Deep Rolling Imaging Fast Telescope (K-DRIFT), a 300 mm aperture, confocal off-axis freeform three-mirror system designed to detect extremely faint stellar structures formed by galactic interactions. Through the K-DRIFT Pathfinder, we identified three key contributors to PSF broadening—alignment errors, opto-mechanical mounting inaccuracies, and mirror fabrication defects—and achieved a 50 % PSF improvement by correcting low-spatial-frequency errors. In the next-generation K-DRIFT G1, mid-to-high spatial frequency surface errors were found to produce scattering patterns in the PSF. By analyzing mirror fabrication characteristics and conducting optical simulations, we traced these scattering effects to specific tool-path patterns within defined spatial-frequency ranges. We discuss how such fabrication-induced mid- to high-frequency errors influence image quality in freeform telescopes.

Items.Authors: Akie Moritsuka, Naoki Kohara, Toshihiro Tsuzuki, Yukio Katsukawa, Fumihiro Uraguchi, Hirohisa Hara, Toshifumi Shimizu, Jun Matsumoto, Yusuke Kibayashi, Koji Hirose, Akihiro Ando
Items.Title: Analysis of oblique solar illumination under off-nominal conditions for SOLAR-C EUVST
Items.Abstract: The EUV High-throughput Spectroscopic Telescope (EUVST) onboard the solar-observing satellite SOLAR-C uses a simplified optical system with an off-axis parabolic mirror and a concave grating for high sensitivity observation. A pre-slit in front of the slit absorbs and dumps sunlight outside the nominal field of view. However, under off-nominal conditions, such as attitude transitions to safe-hold, intense sunlight may illuminate and thermally load components not intended for direct exposure. To assess these risks, we performed ray-tracing simulations using illumination analysis software. The incident angle was varied around the X and Y axes, defined perpendicular to the optical axis. The most intense illumination occurred when sunlight concentrated by the primary mirror reached either the slit-jaw imager or the +Z CFRP panel of the telescope structure. From our results, we defined the angle ranges requiring special attention and determined the allowable dwell time at each angle.

Items.Authors: Yuk Shan Cheng, Kamalesh Dadi, Jake Charsley, William Newman, Richard McCracken, Derryck Reid
Items.Title: ANDES, the high resolution spectrograph for the ELT: a pilot architecture for the RIZ band frequency comb
Items.Abstract: We present a 15-GHz, offset-tunable astrocomb covering 650–1030 nm, integrating a cw marker through a feed-forward technique for unambiguous comb-mode identification. With the goal of future implementation across different wavelength bands, the system can provide good long-term stability to support high-precision radial-velocity measurements for high resolution spectrograph.

Items.Authors: Pedro Morales
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: RIZ spectrograph evolution and engineering solutions
Items.Abstract: We present the evolution of the RIZ module preliminary design, one of the visible spectrographs of the ANDES instrument for the ELT. Following the 2024 preliminary design, which established a fiber-fed, warm, vacuum-operated, thermally controlled echelle spectrograph inspired by HARPS and ESPRESSO, new analyses identified key challenges in mechanical stability, thermal performance, and mass constraints. Innovative mitigation solutions have been implemented, including optimized materials for weight reduction and enhanced structural reinforcements to meet the precision goals over 10 years. The updated design maintains the long fiber slit for etendue reformatting while improving vacuum vessel integration and seismic resilience on both, the Coude room and the Nasmyth platform

Items.Authors: Audrey Lanotte, Bruno Chazelas, Christophe Lovis
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: RIZ Spectrograph Straylight analysis and uniform flatfield illumination
Items.Abstract: The first generation of ELT instruments includes the optical–infrared high-resolution spectrograph ANDES (ArmazoNes high Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph). Its optical design and architecture must not only deliver a high spectral resolving power (R = 100,000) and broad wavelength coverage, but also ensure stringent straylight control and provide uniform flat-field illumination of the detectors for calibration purposes. In this article, we focus on the RIZ spectrograph, operating between 620 and 960 nm.  We present an analysis of the various straylight contributors within the RIZ optical train, including ghost reflections, diffracted straylight paths, and scattered light. We also describe the strategies foreseen to achieve uniform illumination of the R and IZ detectors.

Items.Authors: Mamadou N'Diaye, Adrien Simonnin, Alain Spang, Christophe Bailet, Philippe Berio, Yan Caujolle, Oscar Carrión-Gonzalez, Gael Chauvin, Andrea Chiavassa, Salvador Cuevas Cardona, Omar Gabella, Stephane Lagarde, Patrice Martinez, Bhavesh Rajpoot, Julia Seidel, Guido Agapito, Giulia Carlà, Enrico Pinna, Chiara Selmi, Mathis Houllé, Arthur Vigan, Paolo Di Marcantonio
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph of the ELT: simulated performance of the CORO module and overview of the high-contrast capabilities for exoplanet observations
Items.Abstract: We present the simulated performance of the coronagraph (CORO) module for ANDES, the ELT high-resolution spectrograph. The CORO design and simulated performance are detailed in the presence of adaptive optics residual errors to probe exoplanet atmospheres with the spectro-imager mode. We show the preliminary simulation results on the predicted contrast and the expected detection performance with ANDES performance unfolded (APU), the simulation tool to determine the yield of exoplanets in emitted and possibly reflected light. The characterization operation of ANDES will be discussed to assess the instrument ability to detect atomic and molecular signatures connected to the exoplanet atmosphere characteristics.

Items.Authors: Alen Khanbekyan, Andrea Tozzi, Anna Brucalassi, Monica Rainer, Alessandro Marconi, Ernesto Oliva
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrometer for the ELT: absolute and relative measurement of focal ratio degradation in optical fibers
Items.Abstract: Focal Ratio Degradation (FRD) is a major source of flux loss in optical fibers used in astronomical instrumentation, affecting throughput and spectral performance. This work presents two experimental setups for evaluating FRD through relative and absolute measurements. The relative setup, based on a LED source and integrating sphere, provides FRD values consistent with reference ring-test data, confirming its reliability. The absolute setup, using a superluminescent diode and direct focal-plane reference measurements, enables the determination of total efficiency, including insertion and Fresnel losses, for different fiber configurations. The strong agreement between the two methods demonstrates their effectiveness for precise fiber characterization in high-performance spectrograph applications.

Items.Authors: Tom Seccull, Ioannis Apergis, Leonidas Asimakoulas, Colin G. Coates, Darren Frew, Jouni Jussila
Items.Title: Andor Toran: a versatile sCMOS camera platform for astronomy and physical science
Items.Abstract: We present the new Andor Toran, a compact, robust, and versatile camera platform designed to support a range of sCMOS sensors. The first Toran camera to launch is the Toran-PS 26B which integrates the 26 megapixel IMX571 sensor from Sony. This large format, high resolution, back-illuminated sensor offers high sensitivity, native 16-bit digitization, and full-frame readout in under 150 ms. With these specifications, exceptionally low dark current, and practically zero amplifier glow, Toran’s first sensor ensures that sensitive, reliable, and quantitatively robust wide-field astronomical survey imaging is supported across a broad range of survey cadences and exposure times with small optically fast survey telescopes. Alongside the properties of the Toran-PS 26B that support its practicality and performance in astronomical imaging, we will outline the roadmap for future development of Toran as a camera platform.

Items.Authors: Nicholas E. Kruczek, Drew M. Miles, Brian T. Fleming, Randall McEntaffer, Fabien Grisé, Kevin C. France
Items.Title: Anisotropically-etched echelle gratings for the far ultraviolet bandpass
Items.Abstract: Modern grating manufacturing techniques suffer from inherent issues that limit their peak efficiencies. We describe work in collaboration with the Nanofabrication Lab at Penn State University to design and characterize etched silicon echelle gratings optimized for the far ultraviolet (FUV; 90 - 180 nm) bandpass. We discuss the improvements to grating performance enabled by this technology and provide updated grating efficiency measurements. The FUV echelle improvements can ultimately benefit the faint source sensitivity and high-resolution performance of future UV observatories, such as the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), by reducing the non-uniform inter-order backgrounds that have historically plagued echelle spectrographs. We additionally discuss efforts that are underway to improve scatter and spectral resolution measurements needed to meet the characterization requirements expected for HWO.

Items.Authors: Andreas Pohl, Simone del Togno, Thomas Säuberlich, Yaquelin Rosas Ortiz, Karsten Westerdorff, Carlos Arcos Carrasco, Dennis Wendler, Gisbert Peter, Ingo Walter, Patrick Dern, Martin Pertenais, Till Hagelschuer, Nils Müller, Ana-Catalina Plesa, Giulia Alemanno
Items.Title: Annealing of radiation damage in InGaAs vSWIR imaging sensors
Items.Abstract: The InGaAs photodetector used in the VEM and VenSpec-M instruments for NASA’s VERITAS and ESA’s EnVision missions has shown high potential for moderate temperature annealing during our space environment qualification campaign. We propose an annealing scenario that could be applied to the detector and incorporates estimations for galactic cosmic rays (GCR) and solar energetic particles (SEP) events, which are the main causes of increased noise and thus reduced image SNR.

Items.Authors: Dani Guzman, Jon Lawrence, Tiger Wang, Michael Goodwin, Andrew Rakich, Timothy Chin, Jessica Zheng, Lew Waller, Helen McGregor, Zhemin Cai, Ali Ghari Zadeh, Chris Coote, Tony Farrell, Summer Luo, Thierry Fusco, Benoit Neichel, Pierre Jouve, Carlos Correia, Julien Charton, Anne-Sophie Bruni Favier, Sylvain Cetre, Celia Blain, Gaetano Sivo, Tim Gaggstatter, Martin Tschimmel, Masen Lamb
Items.Title: AOB: the new adaptive optics bench at Gemini North is reaching Critical Design Review
Items.Abstract: The Adaptive Optics Bench (AOB) for Gemini North is an international collaboration led by Australian Astronomical Optics at Macquarie University. AOB will reach its Critical Design Review in 2025, before entering construction and AIT phases. AOB will deliver near-diffraction-limited performance to Gemini's GIRMOS instrument through dual AO modes: Laser Tomography AO using 4 LGS and 1-3 NGS for narrow field correction, and Ground Layer AO providing uniform correction over a 2' field. Following CDR completion, the project will begin AO subsystems AIT in France, where all AO components will be validated on a dedicated laboratory bench, including observatory control software and real-time computer. Long-lead optical and mechanical items will be ordered, in preparation for final AIT in Sydney. This presentation focuses on the progress of the project, in particular innovation-driven design across engineering disciplines.

Items.Authors: Andrea Meneguzzo, Alain J. Corso, Giampaolo Piotto, Maria G. Pelizzo
Items.Title: Application of a single freeform optic on a three mirror anastigmat telescope on Cubesat
Items.Abstract: Freeform-optics-based telescopes are emerging as a key enabling technology for Earth Observation (EO) remote sensing, offering superior performance, wider fields of view and more compact architectures over conventional optical systems.   This work presents the design and analysis of an optimized f/3.5 off-axis reflective positive–negative–positive three-mirror anastigmatic (PNP-TMA) telescope operating in the visible range (400–800 nm), where a freeform surface is applied to the tertiary mirror. The introduction of a sixth-order XY polynomial freeform surface enables diffraction-limited performance over a ±6° field of view, along the X-direction. Considerations on dispersive elements are addressed for hyperspectral imaging applications targeting urban and vegetation monitoring.

Items.Authors: Stefan Kuiper, Matias Kidron, Bert Dekker, Gemma Neroni, Jan de Vreugd, Ramon Rijnbeek, Raquel Fernandez Delicado, Max Baeten, Wouter Jonker, Matthew Maniscalco, Philip Hinz, Aaron Hunter, Matt Radovan, Emily Plume, Deno Stelter, Maureen Savage, Antonin Bouchez, Eduardo Marin
Items.Title: Architectural design of the Keck Adaptive Secondary Mirror
Items.Abstract: Keck Observatory is upgrading the Keck I telescope with an Adaptive Secondary Mirror (KASM) for ground-layer adaptive optics (GLAO). TNO was selected to develop the preliminary design using its Hybrid Variable Reluctance (HVR) actuator technology, known for high force output and efficiency. KASM will incorporate ~3,200 actuators across a Ø1450 mm aperture, a major scale-up from previous ASMs (UH88 ASM: 204 actuators, Ø620 mm). The design features a 3 mm thick borosilicate convex mirror shell connected via rods to HVR actuators, supported by a silicon-carbide backing for thermal stability and dynamic performance. Integrated driver electronics reduce cabling, and a hexapod ensures precise alignment. Current efforts focus on architecture definition, performance analysis, and breadboarding activities for mirror manufacturing, integration, and servicing. This paper outlines the latest design status, key considerations, and future development plans.

Items.Authors: Guillermo Bravo Guinea, Niels Christian Jessen, Søren M. Pedersen, Damir Ljubičić, Desiree Della Monica Ferreira, Lars A. Buchhave
Items.Title: ARIEL bipods technical status and mechanical–thermal performance of flexures
Items.Abstract: The ARIEL mission's spacecraft employs a bipods structure made of CFRP, titanium, and aluminum to support and thermally isolate the telescope. This paper outlines the current bipod design status at DTU Space. The bipods must combine high stiffness to prevent modal coupling with sufficient flexibility to accommodate thermal distortions. This dual requirement is achieved through cylindrical flexures whose geometry critically affects the mechanical and thermal performance of the bipods. Analysis results evaluating the impact of flexure geometry on stiffness, strength, and thermal conductance are also presented. These results can be used as a guide for future flexure design of optical instrument structures.

Items.Authors: Eitan Péchevis, Jérôme Amiaux, Clara Bataillon, Marion Baumann, Michel Berthé, Thomas Capocci, Christophe Cara, Cyrille Delisle, Elsa Ducrot, Jean Fontignie, Benoit Horeau, Duc-Dat Huynh, Grégory Kaszubiak, Pierre-Olivier Lagage, Isabelle Le Mer, Nathan Leguay, Michel Lortholary, Jérôme Martignac, Thibault Pichon, Léna Provost, Bastien Reboul, Diana Renaud, Thierry Tourrette, François Visticot, Damien Bachet, Nicolas Berton, Christophe Cossou, Mickaël Lacroix, Hervé Le Provost, Virgile Meyer, Lexane Picault, Nicolas Solenne, Antoine Arondel, Stéphane Correia-da-Costa, Bruno Crane, Jean-Pierre Dubois, Norma Hurtado, Clémence De Jabrun, François Langlet, Benoît Lecomte, Antoine Maillot, Marc Ollivier, Anne Philippon, Catherine Tamiatto, Stéphane Tosti, Xue Yan Zhang, Eric Gendron, Yanis Gougeat, Vincent Lapeyrere, Jérôme Parisot, Jean-Michel Reess, Didier Zeganadin, Alain Triffaux, Jean-Christophe Bouquier, Daphné Caillot, Fabrice Glize, Pascal Truchelut, Jean-Philippe Beaulieu, Pierre Drossart, Angèle Sity, Pierre Vigneron, Isabelle Zenone, Elisa Baldit, Pascale Danto, Hervé Geoffray, Gaëlle Giesen, Elodie Jacquel, Oceane Maisonnave, Florian Lazartigues, Paul Eccleston, Enzo Pascale, Adrien Défossé, Mallaury Guerrier
Items.Title: Ariel InfraRed Spectrometer (AIRS): performance of the full instrument engineering model
Items.Abstract: ARIEL IR Spectrometer (AIRS) is the infrared spectroscopic instrument of the ARIEL mission providing spectroscopy based on two independent channels covering the CH0 [1.95-3.90] µm and the CH1 [3.90-7.80] µm wavelength. The instrument is producing spectrum of low resolutions R>100 in CH0 and R>30 in CH1 on two independent Teledyne H1RG detectors. The Engineering Model is the first model fully representative in terms of performance of the full instrument chain, from optical to detection chain performance. The test bench and the results of the AIRS Engineering Model full instrument characterization of performance are presented in this paper covering the optical and detection chain in a representative environment of the mission.

Items.Authors: Anna Brucalassi, José Antonio Araiza-Durán, Paolo Picchi, Andrea Tozzi, Andrew Caldwell, Andrea Bocchieri, Enzo Pascale, Camille Galy, Andres Garcia Pérez, Alejandro Jose Fernandez, Gianluca Morgante, Javier Pérez Álvarez, Davide Bruzzi, Martin E. Caldwell, Vincenzo Davide Cardinale, Paolo Chioetto, Fabio D'Anca, Paul Eccleston, Daniele Gottini, Elisa Guerriero, Riccardo Lilli, Giuseppe Malaguti, Giuseppina Micela, Angelo Olivieri, Emanuele Pace, Giampaolo Preti, Giorgio Savini, Antonio Scippa, Giovanna Tinetti, Paola Zuppella
Items.Title: ARIEL Payload STOP Analysis: updated results on the in-flight operational cases for the Telescope Assembly
Items.Abstract: At payload level, a Structural, Thermal, and Optical Performance (STOP) analysis is carried out to evaluate how thermo-elastic effects may impact the instrument’s optical performance. A STOP analysis integrates structural, thermal, and optical models to predict how temperature variations and mechanically induced deformations propagate through the telescope assembly and ultimately affect key optical metrics such as alignment, wavefront error, and imaging quality. This coupled approach enables the estimation of performance degradation under representative environmental load cases and supports verification of compliance with scientific and engineering requirements.    This document presents the updated results of the optical design analysis performed to predict the in-flight performance for the Telescope Assembly of the ESA M4 mission Ariel according to the operational scenarios defined for Cycle C-2.

Items.Authors: Carlos J. Vargas, Haeun Chung, Erika Hamden, Aafaque Khan
Items.Title: Aspera spectrograph integration and environmental testing: lessons from developing a university-led FUV SmallSat
Items.Abstract: The warm-hot circumgalactic medium (CGM) represents a dominant baryonic reservoir in galaxies, yet remains unmapped in emission due to the technical challenges of detecting faint O VI emission lines. Aspera addresses this through a dual-channel far ultraviolet (FUV) spectrograph design combining enhanced LiF-coated optics with an advanced microchannel plate detector to achieve the sensitivity required for CGM emission mapping.  We present results and lessons learned from Aspera's payload integration and environmental testing campaign being conducted at University of Arizona facilities. The integration phase required maintaining precision optical alignment tolerances while implementing comprehensive contamination control protocols to preserve the performance of humidity-sensitive FUV coatings throughout assembly and testing. We will also discuss our testing schemes and results from our thermal vacuum testing and vibration testing of the fully assembled flight instrument.

Items.Authors: Yu Ding, Chen Xu, Dongsheng Niu, Xiaojun Zhou
Items.Title: Assembly and alignment of the multiplexed survey telescope wide field corrector
Items.Abstract: The 6.5m MUltiplexed Survey Telescope(MUST) proposed by Tsinghua University adopts a multiple-element widefield corrector (WFC) to achieve large field of view. The WFC consists of five large lenses, two of which are wedge-shaped lenses and act as an atmospheric dispersion corrector. The first lens element has a diameter of 1. 6 meters, while the diameters of the remaining elements range from 1.36 to 1.45 meters. To meet the excellent image quality, each lens was aligned to be well within 20μm and 9arcsec, which is a major challenge. This will be achieved by using a centration measurement instrument supplemented by contact metrology methods. The centration measurement instrument is based on self-collimating imaging principle, with a maximum test diameter of 2m and an accuracy of 2μm. This paper details the design of the large centration measurement instrument, outlines the alignment and assembly procedures and presents the latest results.

Items.Authors: Ellen Schallig, Gavin Dalton, Ian Lewis, Menno de Haan, Rik ter Horst, Johan Pragt, Eddy Elswijk, Elfi Dijkstra, Remko Stuik, Scott Trager
Items.Title: Assembly, integration and testing of the WEAVE LIFU
Items.Abstract: WEAVE is the new wide-field spectroscopy facility for the prime focus of the William Herschel Telescope in La Palma, Spain. It includes a large integral field unit (LIFU), which has a size of 90” x 78” on sky with a resolving power of up to R = 10000. The fibre bundle consists of 600 optical fibres in a hexagonal array; each fibre is 33 m long and has a core size of 0.16 mm.  In this paper, we describe the final design of the LIFU, details of the assembly process on both the input (sky) and the output (spectrograph) ends of the fibre bundle at NOVA Dwingeloo, integration into the WEAVE instrument, and preliminary performance on sky. WEAVE with the LIFU as its main mode has already produced several surprising discoveries, and with five years of surveys to come, will add many more.

Items.Authors: Aashia Rahman, Anna M. Weiß, Carlos Enrique Rodriguez Alvarez, Ria G. Krämer, Kalaga Madhav, Xijie Luo, Stefan Nolte
Items.Title: Athermal package for OH-emission filters for ground-based astronomy: part III: stability assessment
Items.Abstract: Fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) are promising hydroxyl (OH) line filters for ground-based NIR astronomy, but effective suppression requires thermal stability within the tolerance set by the resolving power (R) of the spectrograph used. We analyzed the stability of 20 FBG notches matched to OH lines between 1540 nm and 1590 nm, arranged in five arrays. Four arrays were conventionally mounted on aluminum plates without temperature compensation, while one was housed in an in-house-manufactured athermal package. Using a broadband source and an optical spectrum analyzer (R ≈ 77,500), we assessed short-term and long-term stability across 24°C to 29°C. The athermalized array showed significantly improved wavelength stability compared with the conventional mounts, underscoring the importance of thermal compensation. Accelerated temperature cycling (25°C to 29°C, 3 cycles/2 h) using an in-house astrophotonic spectrograph (R ≈ 10,000) further demonstrated negligible drift. On-sky tests will follow.

Items.Authors: Marco Barbera, Ugo Lo Cicero, Michela Todaro, Federico Fiorentino, Luisa Sciortino, Caterina Tortorici, Fabio D'Anca, Edoardo Alaimo, Andrea Delfini, Christian Circi, Alessia Di Giacomo, Salvatore Varisco, Alberto Gulizzi, Claudio Saitta, Pekka T. Torma, Bahawal Haq, Pascal Mercere, Paulo Da Silva, Fabio Reale, Gabriele Cozzo, Daniele Brienza, Denise Perrone, Marco Stangalini, Paul Boerner, Bart De Pontieu
Items.Title: Atomic oxygen and UV irradiation of metal-coated CNT-based optical blocking filters developed for the NASA Midex Solar Mission MUSE
Items.Abstract: The NASA MIDEX solar mission MUSE (launch in 2027) will observe the solar corona and transition region in the EUV band with two instruments: a multi-slit Spectrograph (SG) and a Context Imager (CI). MUSE will operate for two years in LEO at an altitude of 640 km. During the mission lifetime, the optical blocking filters, mounted on the entrance pupil of the telescopes, will be exposed to atomic oxygen (AtOx) and UV solar light.   In this paper, we report the results of irradiation tests with AtOx, at a fluence equivalent to the MUSE mission lifetime in LEO, with or without solar UV radiation, performed on a set of filters based on a Carbon NanoTube (CNT) pellicle coated with Al or Zr, developed for MUSE as part of the Italian contribution to the NASA mission supported by the Italian Space Agency.

Items.Authors: Tony D. Travouillon, Jeff Cooke, Matt Radovan, Adam Nagy-Sochcki, Victoria Zinnercker, Chris Stokes-Griffin, Adam Lilleyman, Shanti Krishnan
Items.Title: Automated Fiber Placement (AFP) carbon composite camera barrel prototype for the Keck Wide Field Imager
Items.Abstract: The Keck Wide-Field Insturment is an Australian led instrument proposed for the Keck telescope to unlock its wide-field potential in the near UV part of the spectrum. Since it will be placed at the prime focus of the telescope, the instrument had to significantly be reduced in weight in order to minimise flexure. This required using new materials and methodology to build it major compnents.    New Frontier Technology designed and manufactured a thermoplastic composite conical lens barrel for the Keck Wide Field Imager, featuring near-zero axial coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) (< 0.5ppm) and radial CTE (16.2 ppm) tuned to match aluminium mirror mounts. These precise thermal properties were achieved through laser-assisted automated fibre placement (AFP), which enables careful tuning of CTE via deliberate fibre orientation. The final demonstrator has a mass of 5.5 kg, representing an almost fourfold reduction compared with an equivalent aluminium design.

Items.Authors: Veronika Wimmer, Matteo Accardo, Camilo Avilés, Paulo Ferreira, Marcus Haug, Gerd Jakob, Tobias Müller, Rodrigo Olguin
Items.Title: Automated liquid nitrogen supply 2.0 at the European Southern Observatory
Items.Abstract: ESO operates several telescopes in the Atacama Desert in Chile, including the Paranal Astronomical Observatory (PAO) and the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). All VLT and ELT instruments require powerful cryogenic cooling systems for pre-cooling and / or steady state operation to cool masses ranging from several kilograms to several tons.  This paper provides an overview of the fully operational automated Liquid Nitrogen Infrastructure (LIN IS) at ESO Headquarter in Germany, of the ELT LIN IS, which successfully passed the final design phase in 2025, and of the Phase A study for upgrading the PAO site's liquid nitrogen infrastructure similar as developed for ESO HQ and the ELT. The upgrade would entail installing a centralized, fully automated, open-loop LIN cooling system refilling all VLT cryogenic instruments to enhance operational efficiency and safety, minimize manual intervention, and align with concepts developed for HQ and ELT LIN IS, but adapted specifically for the VLT.

Items.Authors: Daksh Singh, Ting S. Li, Sarik Jerma, Shaojie Chen
Items.Title: Automated multi-stressor optical fiber focal ratio degradation and throughput characterization system for future massive multiplex spectroscopic survey
Items.Abstract: Future spectroscopic survey facilities such as the Spec-S5 and Wide-Field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST) will contain over 25000 optical fibers. Characterizing the Focal Ratio Degradation (FRD) and throughput for all fibers will be very time-consuming but scientifically critical for spectroscopic calibration and sky subtraction to maximize the science impact. In this work, we present an automated “multi-stressor” optical fiber FRD and throughput characterization system to speed the characterization of these metrics for individual optical fibers. This system can determine how FRD and throughput are affected by incident angle, the wavelength of the light source, the optical fiber's bend radius, twists in the optical fiber, and external pressure exerted on the optical fiber. We tested the functionality of this system using a variety of single fibers and fiber bundles. The FRD and throughput profiles that resulted from testing these optical fibers under various stressors are presented.

Items.Authors: Thomas Procter, Megan Dubay, Nicholas Law, Hank Corbett, William Marshall, Alan Vasquez Soto, Alex Bucheli, Jonathan Carney, James Dockery, Shannon Fitton, Lawrence Machia, Michael Ronco, Donovan Schlekat, Glenn Walters
Items.Title: Automated optical acceptance testing for Argus Array commissioning
Items.Abstract: The Argus Array is transitioning from its prototype phase to the production of a 1,200-telescope system designed to monitor 8,000 square degrees of the night sky. To ensure the quality of this large-scale deployment and optimize for survey depth, the team has developed an automated acceptance testing system for the Optical Tube Assemblies (OTAs). This system is designed to be a multi-point-source artificial star projector paired with custom Python software to autonomously vet incoming OTAs. Key features include off-axis point generation for sensor tip-tilt corrections, collimation measurements using a Hartman mask, and throughput verification. Additionally, the system employs a dynamic mount to test each OTA under the specific gravity vectors it will experience in the final array, ensuring critical performance standards are met before commissioning.

Items.Authors: James McKevitt
Items.Title: Baffle and filter design for the short-wavelength camera on SOLAR-C EUVST
Items.Abstract: SOLAR-C, launching in 2028 with the Extreme Ultraviolet High-Throughput Spectroscopic Telescope (EUVST) will deliver EUV spectroscopy of the solar atmosphere with unprecedented temperature coverage and resolution. We present the optical design and mechanical impacts for the short-wavelength camera, and how our design choices affect scientific performance using complete forward modelling. We discuss the design and optical impact of the thin-film aluminium filter and supporting mesh, including diffraction and shadowing effects in spectral and spatial dimensions. We analyse this using physical-optics propagation and analytical modelling, and quantify the scientific impact using forward modelling driven by a simulated solar atmosphere. We address the vulnerability of thin-film filters during launch depressurisation with analytical venting models validated using vacuum chamber testing. We describe the stray-light baffle design and low-scatter coatings which suppress visible stray light.

Items.Authors: Eden A. McEwen, Jared R. Males, Elena Tonucci, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Olivier Guyon, Joseph D. Long, Logan Pearce, Laird M. Close, Warren B. Foster, Kyle Van Gorkom, Alex D. Hedglen, Parker T. Johnson, Maggie Y. Kautz, Jay K. Kueny, Jialin Li, Joshua Liberman, Miles Lucas, Jennifer Lumbres, Matthijs Mars, Tiffany Nguyen, Avalon L. McLeod, Lauren Schatz, Katie Twitchell
Items.Title: Beta Pic b in the blue: high contrast detections from 0.6–0.9µm with MagAO-X
Items.Abstract: Direct imaging of young, self-luminous planets provides key insights into atmospheric composition, chemistry, and ultimately formation histories. The beta Pic system is an invaluable laboratory for understanding planet formation with two exoplanets assumed to have formed simultaneously. Photometry in the optical (λ < 1 µm) is especially powerful at constraining Teff due to the rapid spectral drop-off at shorter wavelengths. The Magellan Extreme Adaptive Optics (MagAO-X) visible light extreme AO instrument on the 6.5m Magellan Clay telescope is uniquely capable of high contrast and small inner working angle from wavelengths 0.4-1.0µm. We present the recent visible observations of beta Pic b with MagAO-X and the technology development that has enabled them. We also discuss the characterization of beta Pic c in z’ using the PIAACMC.

Items.Authors: J. Alan Schier
Items.Title: Broadband vibration control using an inertial actuator
Items.Abstract: We investigate using an inertial actuator to actively attenuate mechanical vibrations. We want broadband performance where “broadband” means multiple octaves in frequency.    We start with an analysis of the fundamental behavior of a model system and its closed-loop control, and then test a hardware system that represents a cryogenic cooler mounted on a spring suspension. This is something that might be found on an instrument used on a large astronomical telescope.    The tests results show appreciable vibration attenuation over more than 3 octaves. This is despite the presence of resonances and other dynamics not considered in the analytical model. Additionally, neither the analytical nor hardware controller required sensitive tuning to the plant dynamics, and both systems are unconditionally stable.

Items.Authors: Thansita Thomrungpiyathan, Samaporn Tinyanont, Matthew Radovan, Ryan Foley, Pornapa Artsang, Renate Kupke, Bradford Holden, Daniel Espinosa, Kishore Patra, William Deich, Panyathonnat Panya, Kenwit Phimprasong, Chantira Boonsri, Pakawat Prasit, Maureen Savage, Brian Peterson, Supachai Awiphan, Wiphu Rujopakarn
Items.Title: Building a large K-mirror image derotator and phase I instruments for the Dual-beam Automatic Rapid Transient spectrograph at the APF Telescope
Items.Abstract: The Dual-beam Automatic Rapid Transient Spectrograph (DARTS) is a high-sensitivity, low-resolution (R ~ 700) robotic spectrograph for the 2.4-meter Automated Planet Finder (APF) telescope at Lick Observatory, designed for time-domain astronomy. We present the progress of the Phase I risk reduction system to evaluate the risk of the large K-mirror image derotation system and test automated target acquisition and tracking, consisting of a K-mirror derotator, an adjustable truss structure for alignment, a slit-viewing camera, and an enclosure. We present the final mechanical design, the construction and testing at the National Astronomical Research Institute of Thailand (NARIT), and the progress of its installation at the APF.

Items.Authors: Francis Fortin, Jean-Luc Atteia, Alix Nouvel de la Flèche, Hervé Valentin, Olivier Boulade, David Corre, Damien Turpin, Aurélia Secroun, Stéphane Basa, François Dolon, Johan Floriot, Jean-François Leborgne, Alan Watson, William Lee
Items.Title: CAGIRE: capturing gamma-ray burst infrared emission
Items.Abstract: CAGIRE (CApturing Gamma-ray burst InfRared Emission) is a near-infrared imager that will be mounted on the 1.3m COLIBRI telescope in the San Pedro Martir Observatory. One of its main goals is to follow-up gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) seen by the SVOM satellite and provide J and H band lightcurves of the fading afterglows. The robotic telescope combined with the VHF link with the satellite will allow CAGIRE to arrive very early on target (1 min. after the burst alerts). This is an ideal setup to maximize the chances of catching far away events (z > 6), produced by the first generation of stars (pop III) and thus probe the very early universe. CAGIRE will be operational by the end of 2026 and for a duration of 10 years.

Items.Authors: Gabriel Tayama, Denis Brousseau, David Aikens, Sudharsan Kalidoss, Ram Mohan Telikicherla, Abhishek Patkar, Vikas Chandan, Sreekar Karnati, Xiaopeng Li, Ben Walleshauser, Catherine Croson, Zebadiah Miles, Zhiyong Wang, Greg Radighieri, Dhanushkodidurai Mariappan, Simon Thibault
Items.Title: Capillary-operated stable mesoporous optical system (COSMOS): design update for the Zenith-DARPA program
Items.Abstract: We report recent progress on the COSMOS tiltable liquid mirror, developed under the DARPA Zenith program by GE Vernova in collaboration with Université Laval and Savy Optics. This scalable, non-rotating liquid mirror system features a dual-layer configuration: a ferrofluid base for magnetic actuation and a silver nanoparticle monolayer for high reflectivity. Surface shape and optical quality are actively controlled through capillary/adhesion and magnetic body forces generated by three separate sets of electromagnetic coils operating in a closed-loop enviroment with a deflectometry-based wavefront sensor. In this work, we present the construction and performance of up to 18 cm diameter prototype. We demonstrated closed loop operation with tilting up to 1 degree and the ability to achieve a liquid surface with 10 meters radius of curvature.

Items.Authors: Benoît Neichel, Francisco Oyarzun, Thierry Fusco, Julien Charton, Jean-Luc Gach, Fabien Clop, Yann Wanwanscappel, Lucie Maillet, Christophe Pravert, Piero Bruno, David Boutolleau, Cedric Bremond, Alexandre Lorenzi
Items.Title: Cassiopee: defining the next-generation deformable mirror and high-speed SWIR camera for adaptive optics applications
Items.Abstract: Future Adaptive Optics (AO) for astronomy, optical communications, space surveillance, and defense require ultra-fast, high-precision components. We introduce a systematic method to define performance specifications for two such technologies: a large-format, high-cadence SWIR camera and a high-order deformable mirror (DM).    Using representative use-cases—including exoplanet imaging, free-space optical links, and satellite tracking—we build AO error budgets that drive quantitative requirements for DM architecture and camera performance. These specifications guide the design of a dedicated laboratory testbed for full AO-loop validation.    Finally, we outline the roadmap toward on-sky tests with the EKARUS facility at Asiago Observatory, enabling end-to-end demonstration and paving the way for next-generation AO systems on large telescopes and optical links.

Items.Authors: Ronan Higgins, Stephen Parshley
Items.Title: CCAT: using a laser metrology system for mirror panel alignment
Items.Abstract: The Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST) is a 6-m telescope under construction by the CCAT consortium at 5600 m on Cerro Chajnantor. Designed for observations from 100 GHz to 1.5 THz, it targets a total wavefront error below 10.7 μm. Meeting the wavefront requirements depends on precise alignment of the mirrors and mirror panels. A laser metrology system will measure these alignments with 2 μm accuracy. Because the enclosure rotates in elevation with the mirrors, alignment can be measured at all elevation angles—an advantage over techniques such as holography or photogrammetry. This real-time system enables characterization of gravity and thermal effects. We present the system design, system testing in Germany, and initial results from Chile.

Items.Authors: Olaf Dambon, Clemens Dicke, Jessica Nelson
Items.Title: Challenges in the fabrication of large aluminum mirrors by means of diamond turning
Items.Abstract: The fabrication of large aluminum mirrors for astronomical instrumentation involves significant optical, mechanical, and thermal challenges. Aluminum enables lightweight structures and efficient machining, yet achieving high‑precision surfaces through diamond turning becomes increasingly demanding with growing mirror size. This contribution outlines key factors influencing manufacturing quality, focusing on material behavior, thermal treatment, and stress‑relief processes that affect dimensional stability. Strategies for optimizing diamond‑turning parameters to meet stringent surface specifications are discussed, along with coating‑related constraints arising from substrate microstructure and residual stresses. Insights and results from recent projects highlight both limitations and opportunities for advancing aluminum mirror technology in modern astronomical systems.

Items.Authors: Hagyong Kihm, Ma. Angela Lourdes B. Lequiron
Items.Title: Characteristics of carbon deposition of ion beam figuring method
Items.Abstract: We present the characteristics of a carbon deposition layer formed on a mirror surface during the ion beam figuring (IBF) process. IBF is widely used for precision optics manufacturing due to its highly deterministic, non-contact advantages over conventional polishing methods. However, the sputtered carbon particles from the ion source aperture, which is typically made of pyrolytic graphite, can be deposited on the target surface during figuring. The additive carbon layer must be eliminated, and characterizing its thickness distribution and etch rate is crucial for post-processing. We propose a new footprint model and a dwell time path generation for an adaptive ion beam figuring method that minimizes carbon deposition.

Items.Authors: Nikoli Cooper, Joanna Rosenbluth, Ramya Anche, Kyle Van Gorkom, Ewan Douglas, William Melby
Items.Title: Characterization and coronagraphic performance of a dichroic mirror on a high-contrast imaging testbed
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) is designed to directly image habitable exoplanets with a high-contrast imaging instrument operating from the ultraviolet through the infrared. A dichroic mirror used to create separate wavelength channels may introduce polarization aberrations that degrade the contrast performance of the coronagraph. To quantify these effects, we measure the Mueller matrix of a Thorlabs dichroic using a dual rotating Mueller matrix polarimeter. The dichroic mirror is then installed on the Space Coronagraph Optical Bench (SCoOB) to estimate the contrast performance. In parallel, the Mueller matrix of the dichroic is modeled in Python using polarization raytracing and propagated through a coronagraph with High Contrast Imaging in Python to measure the polarization aberrations of the dichroic in the system. By comparing these two contrast performance measurements, we demonstrate the achievable performance of a high-contrast coronagraph with a dichroic mirror.

Items.Authors: Jehanne Sarrazin, Amira Bouikni, Elsa Huby, Sylvestre Lacour, Mathias Nowak, Jean-Tristan Buey, Manon Lallement, Senol Yazici
Items.Title: Characterization of a J-band integrated circuit for PLANETES, an upgraded high-contrast interferometer for the VLTI
Items.Abstract: Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs) are miniaturized optical systems for stable and compact light manipulation. In Astronomy, they are not yet well adapted for use over a broad range of wavelengths, especially when nearing the visible light. PLANETES proposes to face these challenges for high contrast exoplanet detection, and extend the capabilities of GRAVITY (VLTI) from the K-band to the J-band.  In this talk, I will report on the efforts to design and test a high performance PIC for the recombination of four input beams, including an input dedicated to the monitoring of the instrumental phase variations, a critical step to reach high contrast capabilities. I will present the photometric and interferometric results obtained with our first PIC prototype for PLANETES, characterized on our bench at the Paris Observatory

Items.Authors: Yukio Katsukawa, Yusuke Kawabata, Toshihiro Tsuzuki, Hirohisa Hara, Noriyuki Narukage, Toshifumi Shimizu, Hideki Kato, Luca Teriaca, Udo Schühle, Regina Aznar Cuadrado, Tobias Fiedler, Torsten Feigl, Benjamin Guiton, Shota Narasaki, Akihiro Fujie
Items.Title: Characterization of micro-roughness properties of the primary mirror in SOLAR-C EUVST
Items.Abstract: The EUV High Throughput Spectroscopic Telescope (EUVST) aboard SOLAR-C employs a 28 cm primary mirror with multi-layer coating for 17-122 nm wavelengths. The primary mirror must achieve high angular resolution with high sensitivity and minimal scattering at the shortest wavelength while withstanding 90 °C orbital temperatures, requiring Zerodur for its ultra-low thermal expansion. The required surface figure accuracy is achieved by ion beam figuring, but it may degrade small-scale surface roughness, requiring careful characterization. We used three-scale measurements: interferometry (>1 mm), white-light microscopic interferometry (1 µm to 0.5 mm), and atomic force microscopy (10 nm to 5 µm). These measurements yielded power spectral distributions, which we converted to point spread functions (PSFs) with scattering wings. Reflectivity measurements confirmed consistency with the PSFs. Scientific impact was evaluated by convolving the PSFs with simulated coronal images.

Items.Authors: Tanya Das, Andreas Seifahrt, Jacob L. Bean, Julian Stürmer, Nina Brown, Ze'ev Vladimir, Ritvik Basant
Items.Title: Characterizing fiber and detector systematics of the MAROON-X EPRV spectrograph on Gemini North
Items.Abstract: MAROON-X is an extreme precision, fiber-fed spectrograph on Gemini North, with a resolving power of 85,000 over 500-920 nm. It uses a Fabry-Pérot etalon for simultaneous wavelength calibration and a microlens-based pupil slicer to feed three science fibers that are later combined into a virtual fiber for radial velocity (RV) extraction. We investigate fiber related systematics affecting RV precision, focusing on how focal ratio degradation (FRD) and fiber scrambling influence measured velocities. Using transit data and observations of RV standards, we assess FRD stability, its sensitivity to instrument re-installation, and its impact on flux balance between fibers. We also perform scrambling tests with etalon calibration data to probe sensitivity to guiding and focus variations. Additionally, we characterize CCD charge transfer inefficiency (CTI) and its contribution to the overall RV error budget. These analysis help ensure the long-term stability and reliable performance of MAROON-X.

Items.Authors: Vincent Benz, Wolfgang Gaessler, Jake Pember, Andreas Quirrenbach, Christian Schwab, Julian Stuermer
Items.Title: Characterizing modal noise in high-resolution Echelle spectra using flat-field images
Items.Abstract: Modal noise remains a limiting factor in the stability of fiber-fed high-resolution spectrographs. In this proceeding, we describe a method to quantify spatial frequency modulations and temporal evolution of modal noise using spectral flat-field images. Analysis of the spectral orders reveals structural patterns, which exhibit clear time dependence and vary with fiber core size.  Fourier analysis shows known modal noise characteristics, such as noise being dominated by low spatial frequencies and worsening toward longer wavelengths. These effects are suppressed by agitation and grow in severity for a lower number of active modes. In a worst-case scenario for a static few-mode fiber, peak-to-valley noise levels reach 12% of the mean flux.

Items.Authors: Jiajia Wu, Fujia Du, Jean-Louis Lizon, Qiqige Xin, Kai Zhang
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: environment control system (ECS)
Items.Abstract: The Canary High Optical Resolution Ultra-stable Spectrograph (CHORUS) is a high resolution spectrographic facility for the GTC in La Palma. The facility includes high resolution spectrograph working in the visible band (VIS) and an ultraviolet spectrometer (UVS), The paper presents the Environmental Control System designed to ensure internal optical stability.

Items.Authors: Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Axel Potier, Lucie Leboulleux, Bachar Wehbe, Adam Taras, Anthony Boccaletti, Arthur Vigan, Carlos Correia, Caroline Kulcsár, Charles Sallard, Dimitri Mawet, Elena Tonucci, Elsa Huby, Fernando Pedichini, Gilles Orban de Xivry, Henri-François Raynaud, Iremsu Taskin, Iva Laginja, Jalo Nousiainen, Johan Mazoyer, Jonas Kühn, Julia Seidel, Louis Desdoigts, Lucas Marquis, Mamadou N'Diaye, Matthijs Mars, Maud Langlois, Nicolas Galland, Olivier Absil, Patrice Martinez, Pierre Baudoz, Raphaël Galicher, Raphael Poucelot, Rico Landman, Valentin Fonteneau, Vincent Chambouleyron, Yinzi Xin
Items.Title: Closing the technology gap for the Extremely Large Telescope’s Planetary Camera and Spectrograph (ELT-PCS): development of the coronagraph and focal plane wavefront control strategies
Items.Abstract: The Planetary Camera and Spectrograph (PCS) will be the ELT’s dedicated instrument for exoplanet characterization, with a central goal of discovering and studying rocky exoplanets. To prepare for these ambitious objectives, the PCS R&D consortium, launched in January 2025 under ESO’s leadership, was established to advance the conceptual design and bridge critical technology gaps. We will report on the progress of the coronagraph and focal-plane wavefront control work package. Our efforts focus on the development of coronagraphs tailored for PCS and on strategies for integrating wavefront control into their operation. A key component of this work is the PCS Coronagraph Evaluation Pipeline (PCS-CEP), designed to provide a uniform framework for assessing coronagraph performance and wavefront control, an approach inspired by the Habitable Worlds Observatory coronagraph design survey. PCS-CEP enables a fair comparison of diverse concepts, ensuring a level playing field for innovation.

Items.Authors: William A. Podgorski, Mark Mueller, Colby Jurgenson, Andrew Szentgyorgyi, Cem Onyuksel, Matthew Smith, Abigail Unger, Kenneth McCracken, Daniel Baldwin
Items.Title: Co-alignment of the GMT-Consortium Large Earth Finder (G-CLEF) spectrograph three segment Echelle grating
Items.Abstract: The G-CLEF R4 Echelle grating is a key optical component in the G-CLEF spectrograph. The Echelle grating disperses the light over the 350 nm to 900 nm wavelength range into 111 usable orders which are then cross-dispersed and imaged as echellograms in the two G-CLEF cameras. In order to achieve the required spectral resolution, the G-CLEF grating is 1260 x 320 mm in size. Since this exceeds the maximum size of the Richardson Grating Lab’s production capability, the G-CLEF grating is made from three 420 x 320 mm segments, which are the largest size that can be produced. In order to function as a single grating, the three segments must be co-aligned to arc-second tolerances and must maintain this alignment throughout assembly and operation. In this paper we discuss the novel mechanical adjustment and preloading methodology, which were implemented to rapidly align the grating segments, and the structure which supports the adjusters. We also discuss the alignment and measurement technique

Items.Authors: Chris R. Benn, Lilian Domínguez, Marc Balcells, Cecilia Farina, Nada Ihanec, Nicholas Jannsen, Eduardo Mantero, Javier Mendez, Neil O'Mahony, Yeisson Osorio, Ruben Sanchez, Saskia Schlagenhauf, Lucia Suarez, Gavin Dalton
Items.Title: Commissioning of the WEAVE spectrograph on the William Herschel Telescope
Items.Abstract: A new wide-field multi-object spectrograph, WEAVE, built by an international consortium, has been installed at the prime focus of the 4.2-m William Herschel Telescope on La Palma. WEAVE allows up to 1000 objects (one per fibre, over a field of view of diameter 2 deg), to be observed simultaneously, with spectroscopic resolution R ~ 5000 or R ~  20000. WEAVE also has two integral-field modes, allowing observation of either 20 small fields with diameter 12 arcsec, or 1 large field with diameter 90 arcsec. WEAVE was designed to satisfy the need for large follow-up spectroscopic campaigns complementing surveys by major space (e.g. Gaia) and ground-based (e.g. LOFAR) facilities, and is expected to deliver ~ 10 million spectra over the next few years.    Here we report on the commissioning of the instrument, describe the challenges met along the way, and summarise the current state of the instrument.

Items.Authors: Yu Zhou, Boqi Men, Liqian Xia, Xiaohang Zhang, Tommaso Ghigna, Suerfu Burkhant
Items.Title: Concept design of an ultrafast transition-edge sensor as the detector terminal of a Fourier-transform spectrometer for high-dynamic-range solar observations
Items.Abstract: Mid-infrared spectroscopy near 12 µm enables key diagnostics of the solar atmosphere, but requires detectors with high dynamic range, fast response, and low noise under strong photon loading. We present a concept for an ultrafast transition-edge sensor (TES) integrated into a Fourier-transform spectrometer for solar observations in the 12 µm band. The design targets a 50 µs response with photon-noise-limited performance and sub-µW saturation power using a niobium TES and low-heat-capacity tantalum absorber optimized for mid-IR coupling. Tuned thermal conductance and Tc enable rapid recovery from interferometric modulation. A cryogenic attenuation chain regulates solar loading. A cryogenic HEMT low-noise amplifier provides MHz-class bandwidth to capture high-contrast, rapidly scanned interferograms. This concept demonstrates a feasible path toward high-dynamic-range mid-IR TES devices for future high-cadence solar spectroscopy and imaging.

Items.Authors: Zhuo-Xiao Wang, Song Huang, Gang Ji, Wei Qin, Run-Dong Fan, Li-Quan Guo, Zhong-Tian Tian, Jun-Sen Lao, Pei Li, Lei Huang, Diane C. Kerouanton, Malak Galal, Gloria Mellinand, Sébastien Pernecker, Oliver P. Suárez, Maxime Rombach, Jonathan Wei, Jean-Paul Kneib, Zheng Cai
Items.Title: Conceptual design for the focal plane system of the 6.5-m multiplexed survey telescope for stage-V cosmological surveys
Items.Abstract: MUltiplexed Survey Telescope (MUST) is a 6.5m telescope dedicated to wide-field spectroscopic surveys in the 2030s, motivated by Stage-V cosmology requirements. Under construction in China, MUST hosts ~20,000 6.2-mm-pitch fiber-positioning robots on a 1.2m diameter, aspheric, highly modular focal-plane system, enabling unprecedented multiplexing over a ~6 deg² field of view. We present the conceptual design and performance estimates of MUST's focal plane system. As EPFL is developing MUST's fiber positioning module (FPM) and will report its progress separately, we focus on the scientific requirements, key engineering challenges, and implementation plan for the focal plane system led by the Tsinghua team. In particular, we will present the current plan to satisfy the challenging fiber defocus and tilt tolerance budget and discuss integration with MUST's active optics, the in-situ metrology system for FPM maintenance, and lessons learned for next-generation spectroscopic facilities.

Items.Authors: Itsuki Sakon, Takeo Minezaki, Hiroaki Sameshima, Yuzuru Yoshii, Takahiro Nagayama, Hidehiko Nakaya, Yuji Ikeda, Keiichi Maeda, Masaomi Tanaka, Nozomu Tominaga, Hideyuki Umeda, Buell T. Jannuzi, Peter A. Strittmatter, David J. Sand, Thomas W. Folkers
Items.Title: Conceptual design of the MAGNUM near-infrared four-band imager (MAGNIFI) for 2-m MAGNUM telescope
Items.Abstract: We present the results of conceptual designing of a near-infrared four-band simultaneous imaging instrument—the MAGNUM Near-Infrared Four-band Imager (MAGNIFI)—for installation on the 2-m MAGNUM telescope. The MAGNIFI aims to simultaneously capture the Y (1.032µm), J (1.235µm), H (1.162µm), and Ks (2.159µm) bands. Optical design studies have adopted an F-conversion optical system (F/9.19 to F/6), followed by an Offner relay and three beam splitters to divide light into four channels corresponding to the Y, J, H, and Ks bands, thus realizing simultaneous imaging across 0.9--2.3µm. All channels are planned employ InGaAs detectors manufactured by Hamamatsu Photonics, providing a wide field of view of 3.7 arcmin by 3.0 arcmin. MAGNIFI will enable multi-color, near-infrared imaging contributing to both time-domain and multi-messenger astronomy. In this presentation, we introduce the results of the conceptual design of MAGNIFI and outline the science cases the instrument aims to address.
